subject: Documentation freeze exception + staggered rollout proposal for Q4 runtime feature
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudwhale.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Documentation freeze exception + staggered rollout proposal for Q4 runtime feature

Team —

We need to make a small but critical docs change to the runtime public guide and customer-facing integration steps tied to the new caching behavior that ships in the 10/22 release. Docs is currently in a freeze for the sprint, but the change affects the supported integration examples (prefix caching and KV behavior) and will materially reduce onboarding friction for our two pilot customers (CloudWhale and Acme Retail).

Proposal: allow a scoped docs freeze exception for the "runtime caching" topic only, with the following constraints:
- Docs change limited to one page (integration/runtime-cache.md).
- Changes go through a rapid review: product + security + enablement sign-off within 48 hours of PR.
- Publish behind a feature flag in the guide (marked as 10/22 beta) and link to the stable article once fully validated.
- Staggered rollout: start with pilot customers on 10/22, EU customers on 11/02, broader public on 11/16.

Attachments: staging-schedule.xlsx (proposed gating windows), docs-diff.md (draft changes).

Ask: Laura — can product commit to the 48h review? Stephanie — can enablement coordinate two training slots for pilot CS on 10/20 and 10/21? Samir/Elena — are your teams comfortable with a feature-flagged docs update and staggered rollout?

If we don't get the exception, the alternative is delaying the runtime release by two weeks to align with the current docs freeze — not ideal for pilot momentum.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Documentation freeze exception + staggered rollout proposal for Q4 runtime feature

Michael —

Thanks for surfacing. Product supports a scoped exception pending these clarifications:
1) Exact content scope: confirm there are no API contract changes (only examples + guidance). If any API example changes, we need eng sign-off.
2) Rollback plan: if the cached behavior causes regressions, what exact steps do we take to revert docs and flag status?
3) Dependencies: is there any infra gating (config flag or runtime toggle) we need to coordinate with infra & SRE?

I reviewed docs-diff.md quickly — it looks minor and mostly example updates. If Engineering confirms no API change and SRE confirms a toggle exists, I can commit to a 48-hour review turnaround (product + security).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

Agree with scoped exception if we get the 48h turn. A few operational notes from enablement: 
- I can run two 60-minute pilot training sessions: 10/20 10:00 AM PT and 10/21 2:00 PM PT. Please confirm attendee lists (Samir & Elena suggested).
- Need an internal sneak-peek Playbook for CS with change summary (one pager) — can someone own a 1-page TL;DR?
- If docs are behind a flag, we should add an in-doc banner explaining beta status + known limitations.

I can own the one-pager and the CS playbook draft if aditya_rao can provide the short bullets describing behavioral changes by EOD 10/09.

Stephanie Nguyen
Enablement Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Documentation freeze exception + staggered rollout proposal for Q4 runtime feature

Michael / team —

CloudWhale is comfortable with a feature-flagged doc update and the staggered rollout. A few constraints from our side:
- We cannot accept changes that alter the integration sequence more than 24 hours before our scheduled integration window (our infra team needs time to adjust CI if examples change).
- For pilot testing we need the staging schedule by 10/12 so we can reserve SRE time (attached: customer-sow.pdf outlining our pilot scope).

We appreciate the banner idea — please also include a short troubleshooting checklist for cache-related failures (500ish responses and degraded tail latency are our primary concerns).

Samir Patel
VP, Engineering
CloudWhale

Subject: Re: Documentation freeze exception + staggered rollout proposal for Q4 runtime feature

Decision and owners: thanks all for rapid turns. Summary of agreed actions and owners — final sign-off planned by EOD 10/09 so we can proceed with pilot on 10/22:
- Product (Laura): confirm no API contract changes and sign off on docs-diff.md by 10/09 17:00 PT. (owner)
- Engineering (Aditya): confirm runtime toggle exists and provide one-paragraph behavioral bullets by 10/09 EOD. (owner)
- Enablement (Stephanie): draft CS one-pager and schedule two training sessions (10/20, 10/21). Post playbook to the Drive link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xq-example (owner)
- Customer coordination (Michael): circulate staging window and lock pilot SRE times with CloudWhale and Acme by 10/12. Attached: staging-schedule.xlsx, final SOW from CloudWhale (customer-sow.pdf).
- Docs (Grace): apply doc changes behind the feature flag and include banner + troubleshooting checklist; target publish to staging docs on 10/19. (owner)

Related ticket: JIRA-RD-9876 — I'll create the rollout checklist there and tag owners.

If anyone sees an objection to the sequence above, call it out now — otherwise we'll treat this as the plan and move forward.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
